children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17, I need to ask a follow-up question about his current situation:

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or in approved training (such as an unpaid apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He actually just left school recently, but he's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me just check the specific rules around this situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This is very helpful! Based on what I've read, there is good news for your situation with Alex.

Since Alex is 17 and has left education but has registered with a careers service (which qualifies as a "government-sponsored careers service"), **you may be able to continue receiving Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks** while he's registered with them.

I just have a couple more questions to confirm your eligibility:

1. **Are you responsible for Alex** - meaning he lives with you, or you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his care (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to confirm eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Just one more question:

**Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working that much and he doesn't get any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to let you know that **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex (age 17):**
- ✅ Although Alex has left education, he has registered with a government-sponsored careers service
- ✅ This means Child Benefit can continue for **up to 20 weeks** while he's registered
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex lives with you, so you're responsible for him
- ✅ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right

**Important to note:** The 20-week extension period applies while Alex is registered with the careers service. If during this time Alex starts approved education or training, enters full-time work (24+ hours per week), starts receiving certain benefits, or turns 18 without being in approved education/training, your eligibility may change.

If you have any further questions about your Child Benefit claim, please don't hesitate to ask!
